newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury plans further index-linked maturities.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury plans further index-linked maturities.

text.p: The U.S. Treasury plans to issue two further maturities of its new inflation-indexed securities during this year and next, Deputy Assistant Treasury Secretary Roger Anderson said Friday.

Anderson told the Public Securities Association annual meeting that Treasury was still deciding the details but one maturity would be longer, and one shorter, than the 10-year indexed note already issued.

The U.S. government sold $7 billion of 10-year indexed notes last month. There was strong bidding for the securities, whose return is protected from inflation by being linked to the consumer price index.
"We do not know which is going to come first," Anderson said of the new maturities, "...it's really going to depend on market financing."
Treasury wanted to make sure the market was comfortable with its plans to ensure continued success of the instruments.
"Last month's auction was obviously a very good start but there's still a lot more we have to do," Anderson said.
